{{short description|American chemist (1936–1988)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=August 2025}}
'''Devon Walter Meek''' (1936–1988) was an American chemist and professor at [[Ohio State University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Devon Walter Meek Lecture|url=https://chemistry.osu.edu/events/devon-walter-meek-lecture|access-date=2020-07-24|website=chemistry.osu.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Meek, Devon W. - Author details|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=15079198700|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-28|website=Scopus}}</ref>

== Background and career ==
Meek was born in Kentucky, and received his BS in chemistry from [[Berea College]]. His MS and Ph.D. were received at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], where he studied sulfoxide complexes of transition metals under Professor [[Russell S. Drago]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meek|first1=Devon W.|last2=Straub|first2=Darel K.|last3=Drago|first3=Russell S.|date=December 1960|title=Transition Metal Ion Complexes of Dimethyl Sulfoxide|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ja01508a012|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=82|issue=23|pages=6013–6016|doi=10.1021/ja01508a012|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He served for 27 years in the chemistry department of OSU, rising eventually to department chair. Meek's research group studied synthetic inorganic complexes - especially those of the [[Rare-earth element]]s and late metals<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Springer|first1=Charles S.|last2=Meek|first2=Devon W.|last3=Sievers|first3=Robert E.|date=June 1967|title=Rare earth chelates of 1,1,1,2,2,3,3-heptafluoro-7,7-dimethyl-4,6-octanedione|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ic50052a009|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=6|issue=6|pages=1105–1110|doi=10.1021/ic50052a009|issn=0020-1669|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Green|first1=Lisa M.|last2=Meek|first2=Devon W.|date=March 1989|title=Synthesis, characterization and reactivity of alkoxide and hydroxide complexes of rhodium(I) and iridium(I)|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/om00105a013|journal=Organometallics|volume=8|issue=3|pages=659–666|doi=10.1021/om00105a013|issn=0276-7333|url-access=subscription}}</ref> - and spectroscopy.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meek|first1=Devon W.|last2=Mazanec|first2=Terry J.|date=September 1981|title=Determination of structural and dynamic aspects of organometallic and coordination chemistry by phosphorus-31 NMR spectroscopy|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/ar00069a002|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=14|issue=9|pages=266–274|doi=10.1021/ar00069a002|issn=0001-4842|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Meek's papers are held in a special collection of the OSU library.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Special Collections Registry|url=https://library.osu.edu/collections/RG.40.157/|access-date=2020-07-25|website=library.osu.edu}}</ref>

=== Books authored ===
With [[William Thomas Lipponcott]] and [[Frank H. Verhoek]], Meek authored an undergraduate text in 1970, ''Experimental General Chemistry.''<ref>{{Cite book|last=LIPPINCOTT|first=William Thomas|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-hGDzQEACAAJ|title=Experimental general chemistry. [By] W.T. Lippincott, Devon W. Meek, Frank H. Verhoek. 2nd ed|date=1974|publisher=Saunders|isbn=978-0-7216-5788-2|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 1981 - [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Devon W. Meek|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/devon-w-meek/|access-date=2020-07-24|language=en-US}}</ref>

The Meek Lecture, given annually at OSU since 1989, has honored distinguished chemists including [[Dennis C. Liotta]], [[Jay Keasling]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jay D Keasling {{!}} University of California, Berkeley - Academia.edu|url=http://berkeley.academia.edu/JayKeasling/CurriculumVitae|access-date=2020-07-25|website=berkeley.academia.edu}}</ref> [[Ralph F. Hirschmann]], [[Alfred Bader]], [[Allison A. Campbell]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=For President-Elect: Allison A. Campbell|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i36/President-Elect-AllisonCampbell.html|access-date=2020-07-25|website=Chemical & Engineering News|language=en}}</ref> [[Edward J. J. Grabowski]], and [[William Nugent (chemist)|William Nugent]].
